title: A prompt that starts with a path cannot be sent
body:
A prompt whose first character is `/` is read as a coax command (`src/command.rs`). An unknown command shows `no command /name` in the rule under the prompt and sends nothing. So a message like `/home/jack/x is broken` can never be sent. coax treats `/home/jack/x` as an unknown command, and Jack's rule is that a single-slash command never sends.

## Options

- Send the text as an ordinary prompt when its first word contains a second `/`, since that marks a path. Every other unknown `/name` keeps the unknown-command line. Lean: this one, because a path is the usual way a message starts with a slash, and no coax command name contains a slash.
- An escape: a leading space, or `\/`, sends the text as typed.
- Leave it. The user rephrases so the message does not start with the path.
close_reason: Took the first option in 16554a7. `command::parse` reads a first word with a second `/` as plain text, so the prompt sends and no unknown-command line shows.
